result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_kirchhoff_index()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the Kirchhoff index (total resistance) of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24578-L24652){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_kirchhoff_index() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Kirchhoff index is the sum of all pairwise resistance distances: `Kf(G) = Σᵢ<ⱼ Ω(i,j)` It can also be computed from the Laplacian eigenvalues: `Kf(G) = n × Σₖ (1/λₖ)` where `λₖ` are the non-zero eigenvalues of the Laplacian matrix. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Kirchhoff index. Returns `0.0` for single-node graphs. Returns infinity for disconnected graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: O(n³) for eigendecomposition - the Kirchhoff index equals the quasi-Wiener index (Wiener index using resistance distance instead of shortest path distance) - lower Kirchhoff index indicates better overall connectivity - for connected graphs: Kf ≥ n-1 with equality only for complete graphs ## Examples {.doc-examples} A path graph's Kirchhoff index grows with roughly the cube of its size, since resistance distances accumulate over many series connections: ::: {#8a0ffea1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph() path.add_path_graph(4) # Returns 10.0 path.get_kirchhoff_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 9.999999999999998 ``` ::: ::: A complete graph is the most efficiently connected case, so its Kirchhoff index is as low as possible: exactly `n - 1`: ::: {#3012d347 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} complete = ec.Graph() complete.add_full_graph(4) # Returns 3.0 complete.get_kirchhoff_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3.0 ``` ::: ::: A disconnected graph has infinite resistance between components that can't reach each other, so the Kirchhoff index diverges: ::: {#5cff55f1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph() g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") # No edge between A and B # Returns inf g.get_kirchhoff_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` inf ``` ::: :::
